findings.evidence: Lines 99–108 use finiteness only through `isOfFinOrder_of_finite g`. For any group, lines 56–73 already establish `χ 1 = 1` and `χ (g * g⁻¹) = χ g * χ g⁻¹`, which directly implies `χ g ≠ 0`; grep confirms `[Finite G]` additionally appears at lines 111, 117, and 194 and governs the theorems at lines 200 and 221.
findings.fix: Remove `[Finite G]` and prove `χ g ≠ 0` from multiplicativity at `g * g⁻¹` and `χ 1 = 1`; then drop the section-wide finiteness assumption from all affected declarations.
findings.issue: `charHomOfJointEigenvector` unnecessarily requires `[Finite G]`; the same restriction propagates to `charHomOfJointEigenvector_apply`, `exists_charHom_of_iInf_eigenspace_ne_bot`, and the character-indexed spanning/invariant theorems.

summary: The joint-eigenvector character API unnecessarily restricts representations to finite groups, although invertibility of every group element already makes each eigenvalue nonzero.
